newsitem.title: USA: Guidant Q4 sales volume cut by currencies.
newsitem.headline: Guidant Q4 sales volume cut by currencies.

text.p: Guidant Corp said worldwide sales volume growth of 15 percent for the fourth quarter was partially offset by a two percent reduction in revenues resulting from unfavorable currency movements.
Revenues were further reduced by four percent on worldwide product mix changes and international price erosion, said the medical devices manufacturer.

On a sector basis, Guidant said quarterly sales in its cardiac rhythm management business were $151.9 million, up 23 percent over 1995. Fourth-quarter vascular intervention sector sales fell eight percent to $104.9 million versus a year ago.

Fourth-quarter sales in the minimally invasive systems sector were $14 million, up 37 percent over a strong fourth quarter of 1995. Overall gross profit for the quarter was $202.4 million, up 14 percent over last year.
"Continued improvement in manufacturing efficiencies in all business units contributed to the increase," the company said.

Investment in new product development and clinical programs increased research and development expenses 21 percent over last year. Total research and development, selling and general administrative expenses of $129.5 million grew by 13 percent over 1995.

For 1996, sales were $1.04 billion, up 13 percent compared to 1995. Net income and earnings per share increased 48 percent to $149.9 million and $2.08 respectively, on an adjusted basis, when compared to 1995, Guidant said.
